title: QNAP MCP Assistant per-user auth integration
goal: Enable internal users to access the Pro Select QNAP NAS through the official QNAP MCP Assistant with per-user authentication, NAS-wide user-permission semantics, and explicit preview/approval for transfers and destructive actions.
constraints: Use the official QNAP MCP Assistant as the primary/default path to reduce custom code.
Each user authenticates with their own QNAP credentials.
QNAP user permissions are the primary NAS authorization boundary.
Do not restrict NAS access to local cwd or a local case folder.
AnythingLLM users may ask across multiple NAS folders in chat.
OpenCode users may call NAS folders outside local workspace when needed.
No credentials, tokens, sessions, passwords, or API keys in repo, chat, client config, runtime artifacts, or logs.
Download/upload/delete must not execute silently; use preview plus explicit approval for transfers and destructive actions.
NAS admin/system functions remain out of default user workflow scope unless a separate admin-pilot plan approves them.

tasks.title: Discover official QNAP MCP Assistant install, auth, and tool surface
acceptanceCriteria: Document install command, runtime requirements, and client config shape.
Verify whether it supports nasproselect.myqnapcloud.com.
List exposed tools and classify read, write, destructive, and admin capabilities.
Confirm whether per-user auth/session storage is local and non-secret in client config.

tasks.title: Define per-user QNAP auth and credential handling
acceptanceCriteria: Choose official assistant credential flow if it is per-user and local.
Fallback to OS Credential Store only if needed.
No token or password appears in generated client config or logs.
Auth expiry and reauth states are redacted and actionable.

tasks.title: Configure OpenCode and AnythingLLM MCP entries
acceptanceCriteria: OpenCode can launch the QNAP MCP Assistant or thin wrapper.
AnythingLLM can launch the QNAP MCP Assistant or thin wrapper.
Client entries contain commands/args only and no secrets.
The configuration does not artificially bind NAS access to local cwd or fallordner.

tasks.title: Implement or configure preview/approval policy
acceptanceCriteria: Download executes only after preview plus approval if the assistant requires an apply step.
Upload/overwrite executes only after preview plus approval.
Delete executes only after preview plus approval and only when the QNAP user has rights.
If the official assistant cannot enforce this, a thin Pros wrapper/filter is specified or implemented.

tasks.title: Run live smoke tests against nasproselect.myqnapcloud.com
acceptanceCriteria: User auth succeeds for at least one internal non-admin user and one admin user if available.
List/search works across multiple NAS folders permitted by QNAP rights.
Download works through approved flow.
Upload/overwrite preview works and apply is gated.
Delete preview is gated and no silent delete path is exposed.

tasks.title: Update runtime docs and setup workflow
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime manifest reflects official QNAP MCP Assistant as the default when approved.
Setup docs explain per-user auth, nasproselect.myqnapcloud.com, and no-secret config.
Docs explain that NAS access is governed by QNAP user rights, not local cwd/fallordner.
Docs explain preview/approval for upload/overwrite/delete.

tasks.title: Security and regression review
acceptanceCriteria: No secrets in repo, generated configs, runtime artifacts, or logs.
No unapproved destructive tool path is exposed.
Admin/system NAS operations are blocked or documented as separate admin-pilot only.
OpenCode and AnythingLLM config tests pass.

completionCriteria: Official QNAP MCP Assistant is evaluated and either approved as default or rejected with documented fallback.
Per-user QNAP auth works against https://nasproselect.myqnapcloud.com/ without storing secrets in client config.
OpenCode and AnythingLLM can use the configured QNAP MCP path.
Read/list/search/download workflows work for QNAP-permitted folders across the NAS.
Upload/overwrite/delete cannot execute silently and require preview plus explicit approval.
Docs and runtime manifest reflect the selected default and safety model.
Security review finds no Critical, High, or Medium issues.

decisionLog.decision: Use official QNAP MCP Assistant as the primary/default integration path.
decisionLog.rationale: The official assistant is maintained/tested by QNAP and reduces custom Pros File Station code and custom bug surface.

decisionLog.decision: Do not bind QNAP NAS access to local cwd or fallordner.
decisionLog.rationale: The NAS is an external user-selected data space; AnythingLLM chat may span multiple NAS folders and OpenCode may need NAS paths outside local workspace.

decisionLog.decision: Use QNAP user permissions as the primary NAS boundary, with preview/approval for destructive actions.
decisionLog.rationale: Users should be able to use the rights they already have on QNAP, but destructive actions must not run silently through an agent.
